commenti.body:
I completely agree with you and I think Cooper deserves to be even more criticized for this mess.

When I was watching Maestro it seemed to me like Cooper's main objective was trying to be a "great filmmaker" and show everyone how much of a generational talent he is. I don't think he was actually interested in Bernstein beyond the superficial.
It seems to me that most of Cooper's decisions were to serve the audience and his ego then to serve the story. Maestro to me is a pretentious caricature of a "great filmmaker tackling a biopic".

And I'm not calling Cooper a great filmmaker. To me he's just a guy who thinks he's great, but really isn't. Seems to me like there wasn't one signal personal thought involved in the filmmaking process, just the idea of what this supposed "great filmmaker" would choose.

He's the same in the acting department. It all looks superficial and surface level. Like he thinks that empty gestures, prosthetics and an accent are enough to be a "great performer".
Rumor has it that Steven Spielberg was supposed to direct this movie but dropped out
